newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northwest spot power higher, Southwest lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northwest spot power higher, Southwest lower.

text.p: Spot power prices in the Northwest U.S. were slightly higher Wednesday, while Southwest prices slipped a bit, market sources said.
"We had a ton of rain this past weekend. Eventually water will dry up, but the big question is how low temperatures will be in October" said one Portland, Ore. trader.
Next-day prices at the California-Oregon border (COB) were last quoted $15.75-16.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), up from around $15.00 on Tuesday.
Traders said slightly warmer temperatures in California spurred some buying activity by California utilities.
Temperatures in the Northwest are forecast at normal levels for the next week, and heating demand has yet to kick in, regional sources said.

A manager at the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, which operates federal hydroelectric projects in the Northwest, said streamflows are continuing their seasonal decline, and dams are being operated with the aim of achieving end-of-year reservoir targets.
Next-day prices at Palo Verde in Arizona were seen near $16.00 on Wednesday, down from $16.50 on Tuesday.
Oct COB was quoted $15.25-15.50 per MWh, compared with $15.45-15.65 on Tuesday. Palo Verde for October was last quoted $15.75-15.90, down slightly from $15.80-15.90 on Tuesday.
